source_evidence: Leveraged loans also typically pay a variable interest rate. This means that if market interest rates go up, the interest rate on the loan will also increase.
answer: Leveraged loans typically have floating (variable) interest rates, so the rate can change as market interest rates change. If market rates rise, the interest paid on these loans generally rises too, which could help protect a fund from losses when rates increase. This does not remove other risks of the loans or guarantee that the fund will avoid losses.
